newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RMB leaps on expected Momentum boost.
newsitem.headline: RMB leaps on expected Momentum boost.

text.p: RMB Holdings Ltd shares jumped on Wednesday on prospects of a surge in earnings in its subsidiary Momentum Life Assurers Ltd, dealers and analysts said on Wednesday.

They said RMB was also catching up with other banking stocks which have recently experienced a rally on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange boosted by a rosier outlook for South Africa's economic fundamentals.
The financial index has surged nearly 450 points since last week and has ended at fresh highs in the last five trading sessions.
By 1200 GMT RMB shares had gained 450 cents, or 5.59 percent, rising to a new year high of 85 rand after 40,100 shares valued at over 33 million rand had traded.
"Contrary to the doomsday predictions the rand has strengthened, there is a massive inflow of cash and the (January) reserves are at their highest since March last year," a dealer said.
"Towards the end of last year the outlook for bad debt and the economy was bleak. People were talking of the rand trading at five rand (to the dollar)," the dealer said.

But Dave Southey, an analyst at Edey Rogers said the main reason for the surge in RMB shares was that it was playing "catch up" with shares in Momentum, in which RMB holds a 67.9 percent stake, which soared last week on expectations of robust earnings growth in its current financial year.
Analysts said Momentum was expected to show earnings up a strong 40 to 50 percent in the year to June 30, 1997.
Southey said the anticipated jump in Momentum's earnings would come on the back of a growth in assets under management and a turnaround in subsidiary Aegis Insurance company.
He added, however, that both RMB and Momentum appeared overpriced at current levels.
"I think its crazy. The shares are too expensive," he said.
Momentum shares were also trading at a new high of 49 rand. The share has risen by around 36 percent this month.

Traders said that central Reserve Bank governer Chris Stals' comments on Tuesday that interest rates could be reduced later rather than sooner was probably meant to cool off the enthusiasm over banking stocks.
"Investors were extremely bearish last year, now there is too much optimism. Probably Stals was trying to temper the market into a more realistic level," one dealer said.
